body:
TPG is racing to lock in funding for its 1.31 trillion won Lotte Rental buyout after Korea's FTC cleared the deal ahead of schedule.

This article appeared on Signal, a capital markets news service, at 3:14 p.m. on September 2, 2026.

TPG, the global private equity firm formerly known as Texas Pacific Group, is moving quickly to finalize the funding structure for its acquisition of Lotte Rental. The Fair Trade Commission cleared the merger faster than expected, raising the likelihood that the closing schedule will be moved up.

TPG has begun assembling a co-investment fund with domestic and overseas institutional investors to finance the purchase of Lotte Rental (089860.KS), investment banking sources said on the 2nd. The firm plans to pay for the acquisition using the new fund together with an existing blind fund earmarked for Asian investments. Some in the market had expected the antitrust review to take longer, but the FTC's swift approval on the 1st has given a green light to a closing next month. Lotte Group is also targeting completion of the deal within next month after remaining procedures.

The key variable in an early closing is whether the co-investment fund comes together. TPG is currently managing its $5.5 billion Asia VIII fund, raised between 2022 and 2024, but dry powder in the fund is limited, and the firm is expected to begin raising a new fund starting next year.

TPG also intends to fund the Lotte Rental acquisition entirely with equity, without acquisition financing. That makes the co-investment fund, which would draw additional money from outside limited partners, a watershed for an early closing. "TPG has other vehicles, including an Asia mid-cap fund for mid-sized companies in the region, so even if the co-investment fund is not put together early, we don't see a major problem with closing the deal itself," an investment banking official said.

TPG signed an agreement with Lotte Group on the 11th of last month to acquire about 61% of Lotte Rental at 59,000 won per share, or 1.31 trillion won in total. The firm is expected to fund the entire purchase price with equity contributions first, then consider recapitalizing after the closing to recover part of its investment early. "Depending on market conditions, TPG could also move to acquire all of the remaining shares," another investment banking official said. "In that case, it could employ financing techniques that involve borrowing, such as acquisition financing."
